subject: Discovery: observability & evals for TeleHealthCo — next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Reyes <sofia@telehealthco.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@telehealthco.com, Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@telehealthco.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Intro — observability & evals discovery (TeleHealthCo)

Alex — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned before we kick off the POC planning: 

Pain points we emphasized:
- Post-deployment regressions: model updates have caused a 10–15% drop in summary fidelity for discharge notes; hard to trace root cause across prompt variants and model versions.
- Tail latency spikes during morning syncs (08:00–09:30 PT) that affect clinician UX.
- Cost: token spend is growing with larger context windows; we need guidance on caching/batching/quantization tradeoffs.
- Lack of observability into prompt-level success (we currently only log raw requests, no golden-prompt matching or structured evals).

Current stack (high level):
- Upstream: internal streaming proxy -> OpenAI endpoints for core generation.
- Metrics: Prometheus + Grafana for infra metrics; application logs in CloudWatch.
- No dedicated eval pipeline yet; QA runs are ad-hoc.

Success criteria we discussed:
- Ability to detect regressions within 24 hours of rollout (regression alerts tied to golden prompt sets).
- Dashboards that show prompt-level pass rates, latency P95/P99, and token-cost per endpoint.
- Tracing hooks that let SREs jump from a user-visible regression to the exact model/request/kv-cache state.

What we can share to help you size the POC:
- 2 weeks of sampled request logs (anonymized) + representative golden prompts (20–30).
- Slack contact for our SRE: Jamal Ortiz (cc’d).

Goals: confirm next steps and timing. Procurement looped on contract questions. Looking for a 4–6 week POC to validate detection & alerting flow.

—
Sofia Reyes
Head of Product, Clinical NLP
TeleHealthCo

From: alex_martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Reyes <sofia@telehealthco.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — observability & evals discovery (TeleHealthCo) — recap + proposed next steps

Sofia — great to meet you and thanks for the clear summary. I pulled our notes together and added concrete next steps so your team knows what to expect from a POC scope. TL;DR: we can deliver eval-driven regression alerts, prompt-level dashboards, tracing hooks, and cost optimization recommendations in a 4–6 week engagement.

Recap (condensed):
- Primary pain: regression detection + traceability for prompt/model/version combos.
- Secondary pain: tail latency around clinician peak hours + rising token cost.

Concrete success criteria (proposal):
1) Regression detection: automated daily comparison of golden prompt pass rates with configurable thresholds; email + webhook alerts when delta > 5 percentage points.
2) Observability: Grafana + Redwood Console dashboards showing prompt-level pass rate, latency P50/P95/P99, and tokens/response; linked traces from request -> model run.
3) Tracing & root cause: per-request trace IDs that include prompt variant, model version, kv-cache hit/miss, and batching group.
4) Cost guardrail: batch/caching recommendations with expected cost delta estimate for your traffic profile.

What we need from TeleHealthCo to start (priority order):
- Sample: 7–14 days of anonymized request logs + a ZIP of candidate golden prompts (we can accept a shared Drive link).
- Staging access or a curl-level endpoint and a point-of-contact SRE (Jamal, cc’d).
- Success criteria confirmation (especially alert thresholds and target latency SLO).

Attachments I’m sending: redwood-eval-playbook-v1.pdf (POC scope + runbook), telehealth-mmp-template.xlsx (mutual action plan template).

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0: share artifacts & onboarding call (1hr).
- Week 1–3: instrumenting tracing hooks + ingesting logs and building dashboards.
- Week 4–5: golden prompt evaluation, regression alert tuning.
- Week 6: POC review + go/no-go and next steps (Dedicated or Private options).

If that looks right I’ll share a short MMP and a DocuSign PO placeholder for procurement.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | (415) 555-0189
